title: App Store channel
summary: Diceroll's App Store channel page on its Status tab, in the Ship builds accent: one page with Status, Releases, Listing, Sales and Setup; each store lane with the release track that feeds it, what is live and what is next; what customers do (link and QR code); the Sales side's own state and summary; and the store identity derived from the platform pin.
compare: One page per channel with the tabs in this order: Status, Releases, Listing, Sales, Setup. Sales shows here because the storefront side is set up; when it isn't, the Sales tab shows its wizard and the other tabs are unaffected.
The breadcrumb is 'Diceroll › Ship builds › Channels › App Store', the same path as Channels and every other channel page.

The header: the App Store mark, the name, Live as status text (not a pill), then one meta line, 'Store · iOS · ★ 4.6 from 1,284 ratings' (family · platforms, as Steam's header reads; the kit's meta dots, so each dot has equal space on both sides; the star is the 16px ic-star in brand gold, 4px from its number; the API name stays dropped), then Open in App Store Connect, Publish 1.9.0 (primary, because 1.9.0 is newer than what is live and fits) and an overflow that includes 'Not using Diceroll on the App Store'.
The page is in the Ship builds accent (release cyan); green means Live; the Sales tab and card are in the Commerce colour.

Store lanes has one row per lane, with the columns Lane, From release track, Live and Next. The release track is the shared mono chip in the Ship builds accent, drawn as on Release tracks: App Store from stable, TestFlight · Beta testers (external group, 212 testers) from beta, TestFlight · Diceroll team (internal group, 6 testers) from dev, the same groups as packages.release-tracks. TestFlight is a lane of this channel, never a separate channel, and 'track' alone never names a store lane.

Next for the App Store says what Polaris Key already prepared ('Ready to submit: build processed, notes and listing pushed') with a Publish link; the foot says 'Testing lanes get every release on their release track. The App Store itself waits for your typed click in Publish.' with 'Lane map on Setup'.

The read time is shown ('Read from App Store Connect 3 min ago') with a refresh control named 'Read App Store Connect now', which shows a spinner while reading. Recent lists what happened in words and in order, with who did it: uploaded by the release workflow (22 min ago, when 1.9.0 reached Polaris Key), processed by App Store Connect (15 min ago), prepared for review and sent to TestFlight · Beta testers by Polaris Key (14 min ago), Ana Lima's earlier submission.

When App Store Connect can't be read, the Live card keeps its last-known rows dimmed under one line saying what went wrong and how to fix it ('Couldn't read App Store Connect at 10:42: the team key was revoked.' with Replace key), the channel shows Attention on Channels with the same sentence, and the read time says when the rows are from. A team key that fails its check says so in the App card with Replace key.

What customers do shows the store link (the chip truncates in the middle, 'apps.apple.com/app/…id6478123905', so the id survives, with Copy) and a QR code captioned 'Scan with your iPhone' (the download page's words), and where customers see it, in one line: 'Shown on dl.plrs.im/diceroll and each player's Library'. It comes from the same customer-action model as the download page. The rating is not here.

The Sales card is the storefront side in the Commerce colour with its own state (Live), its 28px tile, and Open Sales in its head (no foot): 'Free · 3 offers as in-app purchases' over '41 purchases in 28 days · 1 refunded and revoked'; 'Test purchases on' appears only when they are on.

App identity: bundle id and Apple ID, then one note, 'Both derived from the iOS platform pin' (never typed), and the team with its key's last check. Under 560px of card width (the rail, a phone) the facts stack in one column: Bundle id, Apple ID, Team.
Sidebar: Ship builds open, App Store active under Channels (Channels carries no count), Steam with '2 of 4'.

Phone: Open in App Store Connect moves into the overflow; the tabs sit 18 px apart so all five fit at 390 and at 360, and below that the bar scrolls inside itself with a shaded right edge that shows only while there is more to scroll; the side cards follow the main column; each lane row stacks with small From, Live and Next labels; the lane-map link keeps its own line under the note. The QR code hides (the visitor is already on the phone) and the link chip keeps Copy; the stacked rail cards sit 24px apart, like the main cards; each lane's From label sits on its 24px chip's line. The rail is shorter than the main column at desktop and wide.

Brand v2 shell (lead B2–B5, 2026-10-09): the work sits on the inset canvas with a 3px rule in the page's context accent (full-bleed below 1024); one orientation line (context chip + crumbs, never 'Platform' on a product page, no eyebrow repeating the path); h1 36/44 on a collection, 32/40 on a record, 24/32 on a phone; the one filled primary is ink; focus, hover, checked and selected take the accent of the service the element references (B17), never a status colour; the selected nav item is the subtle fill with a 3px marker; card heads are bands with no numerals; route tabs are an underline tablist with a 3px indicator; tables with filters are one workbench band; weights 400/500/600.
Ship builds is one identity (B5): Release cyan rule, chip, tile and nav marker, the Package glyph, crumb '<Product> › Ship builds'; no per-page green or tangerine.
The rating star is neutral (gold means signing only); the channel icon leads the record's h1 and Ship builds stays the context (one cyan identity, B5).
Preserved (guide Ed. 04): One channel page carries setup, delivery, listing and commerce (the consolidated channel IA)
Preserved (guide Ed. 04): Per-channel retry model is unchanged
Preserved (guide Ed. 04): Ship builds stays one feature glyph

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fixed: store lanes in the glossary's words and the Release tracks story, the shared release-track chip in the Ship builds accent, 'Store' as the family, the rating and QR caption moved, one breadcrumb path and a coherent timeline.

findings.issue: [versus the plan and other areas] Store-lane names, tester counts and words ('Track', 'testing tracks', 'Track map') disagree with packages.release-tracks and the glossary.
findings.resolution: Columns are 'Store lane' and 'From release track'; the lanes are TestFlight · Beta testers (external, 212) from beta and TestFlight · Diceroll team (internal, 6) from dev, as on Release tracks; the foot says 'Testing lanes get every release on their release track' and 'Lane map on Setup'; the Steam setup says 'Lane map: beta → Steam's beta branch, dev → dev'. itch.io follows stable only on Channels and Publish. No macOS appears on these screens; packages.release-tracks still lists a `mac` itch.io channel, which its owner should drop so the story is one.

findings.issue: [visual] Release-track chips in the Updates tangerine, a fourth accent.
findings.resolution: The chips use packages.release-tracks' .trk shape (mono, 700, accent-subtle fill) in the Ship builds accent, so a release track looks the same on every screen.

findings.issue: [copy] 'App store · App Store Connect API · iOS' reads like a duplicate; Steam is an 'App store'.
findings.resolution: The family is 'Store' on every channel (App Store, Steam, Flathub, Microsoft Store).

findings.issue: [layout] The rating sits under What customers do; the QR code has no caption.
findings.resolution: The rating moved to the header's meta line; the QR code is captioned 'Scan with your iPhone', and the card says what the link opens.

findings.issue: [phone] The lane-map link is dropped on phone; the tabs have no scroll cue for 360.
findings.resolution: The link keeps its own line under the note on phone. The tabs are 18 px apart on phone, so all five fit at 390 and 360 (checked at 360: 328 of 328 px); at 320 the bar scrolls inside itself and shades its right edge only while there is more (checked). The compare keeps the 360 check.

findings.issue: [states and realism] No failed-read or failed-key state; processing came before the CI arrival; 'revoked at once' is unclear; breadcrumbs differ.
findings.resolution: Timeline fixed: uploaded 22 min ago, processed 15, prepared and sent 14 (Channels and Publish agree). '1 refund; that purchase was revoked at once'. Breadcrumb 'Diceroll › Ship builds › Channels › App Store' on both channel pages and 'Diceroll › Ship builds › Channels' on Channels. The stale state is a compare item with its exact copy rather than drawn, because the page shows one read; drawing it would hide the healthy rows the page exists to show.

findings.issue: On phone 'com.example.diceroll' touched '6478123905' with no gap, and 'Derived' was printed twice.
findings.resolution: The ids are a .dl.cols.stack (new kit modifier): one column under 560px of card width, so on phone and in the rail the order is Bundle id, Apple ID, Team, and long mono values wrap anywhere. One .source note under the ids reads 'Both derived from the iOS platform pin'.

findings.issue: The rail ran 150px past the main column, against the kit rule that the aside is the shorter column; its rows were padded, the chip cut the end of the id, and the heads didn't align in the tablet row.
findings.resolution: What customers do keeps only 'Shown on dl.plrs.im/diceroll and each player's Library' beside the QR, with the middle-truncated chip under that line ('apps.apple.com/app/' + 'id6478123905'); Sales uses a 28px .icon-tile.sm, so every rail head is 56px, with Open Sales in its head (the kit's new .card-head.one-line keeps it on the title's line in the 320px rail) and no foot; its meta reads '41 purchases in 28 days · 1 refunded and revoked'. The listed trims left the rail about 130px long at 1440, so the rail cards are also .card.compact (16px inset) and the link chip sits beside the QR: the rail now ends at y=1009 against the main column's 1013 at desktop, and 989 against 1013 at wide.

findings.issue: On phone the QR showed where the visitor already is, the stacked rail cards sat 12px apart beside 24px gaps between main cards, and the From labels sat 6px off their chips.
findings.resolution: The QR figure is .hide-phone; the rail is .mk-rail.blocks (new: --section-gap between stacked cards on phone); From is .cell-label.on-chip (new: centred on a 24px chip).

findings.issue: The text '★' doubled the gap after the dot, and the header didn't read like Steam's (family · platforms).
findings.resolution: The meta is the kit's new .meta-seps: 'Store · iOS · ★ 4.6 from 1,284 ratings', even dots; the star is the 16px ic-star (added to the kit's icon set) in brand gold, 4px from the number. Compare item 3 updated.

findings.issue: 'Live on the App Store' restated the page title and its Live status, and two of its three lanes are TestFlight.
findings.resolution: Retitled 'Store lanes', first column 'Lane'; the refresh button is named 'Read App Store Connect now', and the compare adds the spinner while reading. Compare item 5 updated.

findings.issue: Dev lane: show '1.10.0-dev.3 (217)' as one value.
findings.resolution: declined: '1.10.0 (217)' is Apple's version and build, and '1.10.0-dev.3' is the Polaris Key release; Apple versions can't carry a prerelease tag. They are two facts, not one fact twice.

findings.issue: Merge Recent's uploaded and processed rows, and drop the Beta lane's 'Sent 14 min ago' (or the Oct 3 event).
findings.resolution: declined: Recent is a log: compare item 7 asks for each event in order with who did it. Each lane's Live cell carries its date, so removing one breaks the pattern. ux1 judged the overlap tolerable.

findings.issue: Lay the App card's ids in two columns at desktop to save about 70px.
findings.resolution: declined: The desktop rail card has about 272px of content, where the two mono ids collide; that is the bug being fixed. The other rail trims already bring the rail above the main column.

findings.issue: Draw distribution.channel-app-store-stale as its own screen.
findings.resolution: declined: A new screen in a spacing pass. Round 1 recorded the decision to keep it a compare item with exact copy. Raise it for the states pass.

findings.issue: At wide the Recent rows ran about 1100px and the lane table's Live and Next columns sat 300px apart.
findings.resolution: Page capped at 1280 (.page.cap); main column about 830, rail 400. The Recent time is a fixed 96px right column. Rail and main end on their own rows.

findings.issue: At tablet the three bottom cards stretched with 100 to 130px of empty card and the link chip was cut.
findings.resolution: The rail cards no longer stretch (dropped .even); the QR stays and the link chip wraps under it with at least 240px.

findings.issue: Repeated facts: team key checked, 'Both derived from the iOS platform pin', the Live pill twice, three Sales lines.
findings.resolution: Removed 'Team key checked 3 min ago' and the platform-pin line; 'Shown on your download page and in Library'; Live shows once in the header and the Sales header says '3 offers'. The Sales body is '41 purchases in 28 days' with the refund as a muted suffix; '3 offers' is not repeated there.

findings.issue: Phone lane-map link and refresh were on their own line; 'From' was ambiguous; rows had uneven lines.
findings.resolution: Lane map and refresh stay on the title line (.card-head.one-line); the label is 'Track'; a lane's value and its note share one line, so every lane row is two lines.

findings.issue: Cut or reorder the Recent feed, drop the Setup tab, add an error sibling.
findings.resolution: declined: the tab set and states are fixed by the consolidation plan; the error state is a separate mockup item.
